newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $66-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $66-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle were trading slowly by midday Wednesday at $66.00 per cwt, steady with Tuesday's heavy volume, feedlot sources said.
About 1,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week to date number to 75,000, according to USDA.
An estimated 3,500 head sold in Kansas, which brought the week to date figure to 86,400, USDA said.
Most of this week's showlists were close to being sold as packers rounded up as many cattle as they could before another round of severe cold returns Thursday, the sources said.

Feedlot operators were bracing for lower temperatures and blustery winds that could push wind chill readings to -55 F in Nebraska and -30 F as far south as the Texas Panhandle, according to forecasters.
"That wind can be pretty devastating to cattle," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
When severe cold hits, cattle bunch together and everything they eat goes into maintenance instead of weight gains, the feedlot manager said.
